questions.question: What does the term 'Malware' literally stand for, and what is its core purpose?
options: Managed Software — provides automatic patch updates
Mainframe Software — used to manage large servers
Modular Software — used to install browser plugins
Malicious Software — designed to deliberately harm a system
questions.explanation: Malware = Malicious + Software. Koi bhi software jo jaan-boojh kar system ko harm karta hai — data churaana, corrupt karna, ya control lena.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT classified as a type of malware?
questions.explanation: Firewall ek defensive tool hai, malware nahi. Rootkit, Trojan aur Ransomware — sab malware ke forms hain.

questions.question: In the guide's disease analogy, which illness is compared to a computer worm?
questions.explanation: Analogy mein worm ko cholera se compare kiya gaya — jaise cholera paani se spread hoti hai, worm bhi network se khud-b-khud spread hota hai.

questions.question: What was the estimated global financial loss caused by the WannaCry ransomware attack in 2017?
questions.explanation: WannaCry ne 150 countries mein NHS hospitals, Telefónica Spain, FedEx ko paralyze kiya — $4 billion+ ka estimated loss hua, ek unpatched Windows vulnerability se.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed as a recommended defense against malware?
options: Applying OS and software patches promptly
Clicking unknown links to verify if they are safe
questions.explanation: Guide bolti hai unknown links/files pe click MAT karo — verify karne ke liye click karna hi risky habit hai.

questions.question: Your laptop has become slow, an unknown background process is consuming CPU, and you recently installed cracked software from an untrusted website. What is most likely happening?
options: A necessary RAM upgrade is required
The battery is nearing the end of its life
A routine Windows update is running
A malware infection introduced through the cracked software
questions.explanation: Untrusted source se cracked software install karna malware ka common entry point hai — unknown process aur slowdown classic symptoms hain.

questions.question: What does an attacker fundamentally do in a phishing attack?
options: Creates a fake email or website to steal credentials
questions.explanation: Phishing mein attacker legit dikhne wali fake email/website/SMS banaata hai jisme victim apni credentials daal deta hai.

questions.question: Phishing carried out over a phone call is known as what?
questions.explanation: Vishing = Voice + Phishing. Smishing SMS se, Whaling CEOs ko target karta hai, Spear Phishing naam se targeted hota hai.

questions.question: How much money did Evaldas Rimasauskas steal from Google and Facebook using fake invoices (2013–2015)?
questions.explanation: Rimasauskas ne Quanta Computer impersonate karke fake invoices bheji — Google aur Facebook ne actually $100M+ pay kar diya.

questions.question: According to the guide, what should you do if an email urgently demands immediate action, such as 'your account will be closed in 24 hours'?
options: Forward the email to friends for a second opinion
Change your password before doing anything else
Pause and verify independently instead of reacting to the urgency
Click the link immediately to resolve it
questions.explanation: Guide specifically bolti hai — koi bhi urgency feel ho toh ruko, verify karo. Urgency create karna attacker ki common tactic hai.

questions.question: You receive an email addressed to you by name, appearing to be from your company's CEO, urgently requesting a wire transfer. What kind of attack is this most likely to be?
options: Spear Phishing (or Whaling if the CEO is the actual target)
questions.explanation: Naam se target karna aur specific person ko address karna Spear Phishing ki nishaani hai — agar high-value target (CEO) hai toh Whaling bhi keh sakte hain.

questions.question: What happens during a ransomware attack?
options: The network is shut down due to traffic overload
Data is only copied, nothing is locked
The entire system is permanently deleted
Files are encrypted and a payment is demanded to unlock them
questions.explanation: Ransomware files ko encrypt (lock) kar deta hai, phir Bitcoin mein payment maanga jaata hai decryption key ke liye.

questions.question: Which of the following are common ways ransomware spreads, according to the guide?
options: Only through physical theft of devices
Phishing emails, malicious attachments, unpatched software, and RDP brute-forcing
questions.explanation: Guide ke mutabik ransomware phishing emails, malicious attachments, unpatched software, aur RDP bruteforce se spread hota hai.

questions.question: How much ransom was paid during the Colonial Pipeline attack in 2021?
questions.explanation: DarkSide ransomware ne US ki sabse badi fuel pipeline band kar di — $4.4 million ransom diya gaya, east coast mein fuel shortage aur panic buying hui.

questions.question: What does the guide's '3-2-1 rule' refer to?
options: Backups: 3 copies of data, 2 different media types, 1 stored offsite
Network layers: 3 firewalls, 2 IDS systems, 1 honeypot
questions.explanation: 3-2-1 backup rule: 3 copies of data, 2 different media types, 1 copy offsite — ransomware recovery ke liye critical defense.

questions.question: A note suddenly appears on your screen: 'Your files are encrypted. Pay 2 BTC within 48 hours.' According to the guide, what should you NOT do first?
options: Check whether backups of the affected files exist
Disconnect the system from the network
questions.explanation: Guide specifically bolti hai — pay mat karo, koi guarantee nahi ki key milegi hi. Pehla step hamesha isolate karna aur verify karna hai.

questions.question: According to the guide's 'How It Works' breakdown, what typically happens right after ransomware encrypts your files?
options: Files are automatically restored from backup
Antivirus software instantly detects and removes it
A ransom note appears with a Bitcoin address
questions.explanation: Steps: install → files dhundhna → AES-256 se encrypt → ransom note dikhna with Bitcoin address → timer shuru.

questions.question: What is a botnet?
options: A single, highly powerful hacking tool
A network of infected computers remotely controlled by an attacker
questions.explanation: Botnet = hazaron/laakhon infected computers ka network jise ek 'bot herder' (attacker) remotely control karta hai.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common use of a botnet, according to the guide?
questions.explanation: Guide ke mutabik botnet uses: DDoS attacks, spam sending, crypto mining, credential theft, ad fraud — legitimate development inmein nahi aata.

questions.question: What type of devices did the Mirai Botnet (2016) primarily infect?
options: IoT devices such as cameras and routers
questions.explanation: Mirai ne IoT devices (cameras, routers) infect kiye aur Dyn DNS pe DDoS kiya — Twitter, Netflix, Amazon, Reddit US mein down ho gaye.

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use to describe a botnet?
options: Someone is secretly remote-controlling your phone in the background
Someone forces your hand to sign a cheque while you sleep
A disease that spreads in different forms
A postman is secretly reading your letters
questions.explanation: Botnet analogy: tum normal use kar rahe ho, but background mein koi tumhara device remotely spam/attack ke liye use kar raha hai.

questions.question: You notice your router has been sending heavy outbound traffic 24/7 that you never initiated. What does this most likely indicate?
options: The router has become part of a botnet
This is normal background sync activity
The ISP has made a billing error
questions.explanation: Bina wajah heavy outbound traffic — especially IoT device jaise router se — botnet infection ka classic sign hai (jaise Mirai).

questions.question: Why does a server crash during a DDoS attack?
options: The power supply is cut off
Thousands of bots send so much traffic at once that the server cannot handle it
questions.explanation: DDoS mein distributed bots massive traffic bhejte hain jisse server overload ho ke crash/freeze ho jaata hai — real users access nahi kar paate.

questions.question: What is the main difference between DoS and DDoS?
options: DoS only targets websites; DDoS only targets apps
They are the same attack with different names
DoS comes from a single machine; DDoS is distributed across thousands of machines
DoS is more dangerous than DDoS
questions.explanation: DoS single machine se attack hai (block karna easy), DDoS distributed hai hazaron machines se (block karna almost impossible).

questions.question: The 2018 GitHub DDoS attack was the largest recorded at the time. What was its peak traffic speed?
questions.explanation: GitHub pe 1.35 Tbps ka attack hua tha — Memcached servers ka amplification exploit karke. GitHub 10 minutes down raha, phir Akamai ne absorb kiya.

questions.question: Which technique does the guide recommend as a defense against DDoS attacks?
options: Using a CDN (such as Cloudflare or Akamai) to absorb traffic
questions.explanation: DDoS defenses: CDN use karo, rate limiting, Anycast network diffusion, ISP-level filtering — antivirus/password yeh DDoS-specific defenses nahi hain.

questions.question: Your e-commerce site crashes during a big sale, and traffic logs show 50,000 different IPs sending requests within the same second. What is most likely happening?
questions.explanation: Multiple distributed IPs se massive simultaneous traffic — classic DDoS signature, genuine sale traffic itna sudden aur distributed nahi hota.

questions.question: What does an attacker do in a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack?
options: Sends a fake email to steal credentials
Secretly inserts themselves between two parties to read or modify their data
Installs malware on the victim's system
questions.explanation: MITM mein attacker do communicating parties ke beech secretly aa jaata hai aur unka data intercept/modify karta hai bina unko pata chale.

questions.question: What is it called when an attacker sets up a fake WiFi hotspot to intercept traffic?
questions.explanation: Evil Twin = fake WiFi hotspot jo legit se same naam ka hota hai. ARP/DNS spoofing aur SSL stripping alag MITM techniques hain.

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use to explain MITM attacks?
options: A postman opens your letter, alters it, reseals it, and delivers it
Someone is secretly controlling your phone remotely
Thousands of bots send traffic at once
A disease that spreads in different forms
questions.explanation: Postman analogy — letter tumne bheja, par beech mein koi usse open/modify karke aage bhej deta hai bina dono parties ko pata chale.

questions.question: After connecting to free airport WiFi, your banking app login fails and you see a suspicious certificate warning. What is most likely happening?
options: A MITM attack (possibly an Evil Twin or SSL Stripping)
The app simply needs an update
questions.explanation: Public WiFi + certificate warning = classic MITM red flag. Attacker traffic intercept karne ki koshish kar raha ho sakta hai.

questions.question: According to the guide, what is the most common MITM technique used at public WiFi locations like coffee shops or airports?
options: Evil Twin — a fake hotspot with the same name
Recruiting the device into a botnet
questions.explanation: Public WiFi pe attacker Evil Twin (same naam ka fake hotspot) banaata hai — victim connect hota hai, attacker sab traffic dekh leta hai.

questions.question: What does an attacker do in a SQL Injection attack?
options: Enters SQL code into a web form to trick the database
Physically hacks into the database server
questions.explanation: SQL Injection mein attacker web forms mein malicious SQL code daalta hai jo database directly execute kar leta hai bina proper sanitization ke.

questions.question: Why does SQL Injection work in the first place?
options: When a server's RAM becomes full
When a website inserts unsanitized user input directly into a SQL query
questions.explanation: Root cause: unsanitized user input directly SQL query mein jaana — attacker apna SQL command as input de deta hai jo execute ho jaata hai.

questions.question: Typing `admin'--` into a login form's username field can bypass the password check. What concept does this demonstrate?
options: XSS — a script injected into the browser
SQL Injection — '--' is a SQL comment, so the rest of the query is ignored
questions.explanation: Guide ke code example ke mutabik `admin'--` se query ka password-check part comment ban jaata hai SQL mein, aur skip ho jaata hai — classic SQLi.

questions.question: How many credit card numbers were stolen in the Heartland Payment Systems breach (2008) via SQL injection?
questions.explanation: SQL injection se 130 million credit card numbers chori huye, $140 million+ settlement — us waqt US history ki largest data breach thi.

questions.question: What is the primary technique the guide recommends for defending against SQL Injection?
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries/prepared statements user input ko SQL command ki tarah execute hone se rokte hain — sabse effective SQLi defense.

questions.question: What does an attacker do in a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack?
options: Injects malicious JavaScript into a website that runs in the victim's browser
questions.explanation: XSS mein attacker JS inject karta hai; jab victim page open karta hai, uska browser attacker ka script run kar deta hai — cookies/tokens chori ho sakte hain.

questions.question: A script that gets permanently saved in a database (such as in a comment section) is which type of XSS?
questions.explanation: Stored XSS = script database mein save ho jaata hai (e.g. comments), Reflected = URL mein, DOM-based = client-side manipulation.

questions.question: How many profiles did the Samy Worm (MySpace, 2005) infect within a single day?
questions.explanation: Samy Kamkar ne XSS script daali, ek din mein 1 million+ profiles ne automatically 'Samy is my hero' add kar liya — history ka fastest spreading virus.

questions.question: A user posts a script in a forum's comment box that steals cookies, and it gets saved permanently. What is the risk?
options: Nothing happens, browsers block this automatically
Only the commenter's own account will be compromised
Every user who views the page will have their cookies sent to the attacker (Stored XSS)
The forum's database will be deleted
questions.explanation: Yeh Stored XSS ka classic example hai — script database mein saved hai, jo bhi page open karega uska browser script run karega aur cookie chori hogi.

questions.question: What is the most fundamental step to protect a website from Stored/Reflected XSS?
options: Escape or sanitize user input before rendering it as output
Install antivirus software on the server
questions.explanation: User-supplied input ko HTML mein render karne se pehle escape karna (jaise `escapeHtml()`) XSS ka fundamental defense hai.

questions.question: What happens in a CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) attack?
options: The attacker installs malware on the victim's device
The attacker directly steals the victim's password
The attacker floods the server with traffic
The attacker tricks the victim's browser into performing an unwanted action using their active login session
questions.explanation: Tum logged in ho bank.com pe; evil website background mein bank.com ko request bhejti hai tumhare naam se — tumhare cookies/auth use karke.

questions.question: Why does CSRF work?
options: Browsers automatically attach same-domain cookies to every request
questions.explanation: Browser automatically cookies attach karta hai same-domain requests mein — attacker isi cheez ka fayda uthata hai, tumhara browser khud auth kar deta hai.

questions.question: Which analogy does the guide use for CSRF?
options: A postman opens and reads your letter
Someone forces your hand to sign a cheque while you are asleep
Someone is remotely controlling your phone
A disease that spreads in different forms
questions.explanation: CSRF analogy: signature tumhara hai but tumne consciously sign nahi kiya — browser ne unknowingly action authorize kar diya, jaise neend mein sign karwaana.

questions.question: Which technique does the guide recommend as a defense against CSRF?
options: CSRF tokens — a unique token included in every request
questions.explanation: CSRF defenses: unique CSRF tokens har request mein, SameSite cookie attribute, aur server-side origin header verification.

questions.question: While logged into your bank account, you briefly open a random website in a new tab that closes itself immediately. Later, you discover an unauthorized transfer occurred. What likely happened?
questions.explanation: Background mein evil website ne tumhare active bank session (cookies) use karke unauthorized request bhej di — classic CSRF scenario.

questions.question: Why is it called a 'Zero-Day' exploit?
options: The attack completes within a single day
The exploit is sold for zero cost on the dark web
The vendor has had zero days to build a fix, and attackers are already exploiting it
The attack happens with zero seconds of warning
questions.explanation: Vulnerability abhi discover hua hai, patch exist nahi karta — vendor ke paas 'zero days' hain fix karne ke liye, aur attacker already exploit kar raha hai.

questions.question: According to the guide, how much can a zero-day exploit sell for on the dark web?
questions.explanation: Zero-day exploits dark web pe $1M+ mein bikte hain — intelligence agencies bhi buy karti hain, Google Project Zero inhe hunt karta hai.

questions.question: How many zero-day exploits did Stuxnet (2010) use simultaneously, which was considered unprecedented?
questions.explanation: Stuxnet ne 4 zero-days ek saath use kiye — Iran ke Natanz facility mein 1,000 centrifuges destroy kiye bina koi bomb use kiye.

questions.question: A researcher discovers a new bug with no patch available yet, and attackers are already exploiting it in the wild. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Bina patch ke, already-exploited-in-the-wild vulnerability — yehi zero-day exploit ki definition hai.

questions.question: How many of Chapter 1's 10 terms carry the 'Threat' badge in the guide?
questions.explanation: Chapter 1 ('Core Threats & Attacks') ke saare 10 terms — Malware se Zero-Day tak — 'Threat' badge ke saath categorized hain.

questions.question: Based on the guide's severity bars, which of these Chapter 1 threats has the highest listed severity?
questions.explanation: Guide ke severity bars ke mutabik Ransomware 95% ke saath sabse high hai Chapter 1 mein, jabki Zero-day 98% ke saath overall highest hai.

questions.question: In a real attack chain, a phishing email first steals an employee's password, which the attacker then uses to perform SQL injection on the company database. What does this illustrate?
options: Multi-stage attacks — one weak point (phishing) becomes the gateway to a bigger attack (SQLi)
Phishing and SQLi are never used together
This is purely theoretical and doesn't happen in reality
questions.explanation: Real-world attacks rarely single-technique hote hain — chapter ke saare threats ek dusre ke saath chain ban sakte hain, isliye har layer ki defense zaroori hai.
